generalized_heuristic: Classify every citation into its primary structural category (ACADEMIC, WEB_TECHNICAL, NEWS_MEDIA, LEGAL_GOV, or CLASSICAL_CANONICAL) before selecting a resolution tool. Never force non-academic web or news items into academic DOI search tools.
underlying_mechanism: Querying academic APIs with news headlines or software tickets generates false-positive DOI mismatches.
incident_context: Discovered CrossRef querying on blog posts and GitHub issues in early chapter runs.

generalized_heuristic: When resolving academic papers via CrossRef or OpenAlex, accept candidate payloads only when both the primary author surname and key title concepts match. Reject ambiguous fuzzy matches.
underlying_mechanism: Fuzzy API search often returns completely unrelated papers sharing generic words (e.g. 'Language', 'AI').
incident_context: CrossRef fuzzy matching attached mismatched paper metadata to chapter queries.

generalized_heuristic: For web articles, news, and technical posts, verify if the asset is already in Cargo Hold via check_cargo_manifest. If missing, queue the URL for Spyglass seizure and assemble a clean web node with verified publication dates.
underlying_mechanism: Web citations lack permanent DOIs and require full-text seizure into Cargo Hold for long-term provenance.
incident_context: Ensuring non-academic citations are captured in Cargo Hold without journal DOIs.

generalized_heuristic: For legal dockets, court opinions, government reports, or classical philosophical works, preserve specific docket numbers, translators, editions, and historical containers rather than flattening into generic article schemas.
underlying_mechanism: Legal and classical citations rely on specific jurisdictional or translator containers for semantic validity.
incident_context: Preserving court docket numbers and translator names in early chapter references.

generalized_heuristic: Inspect draft URLs for placeholder domains or unrelated repo links. When a placeholder is detected, strip the bad URL, log a telemetry event, and use search grounding to find the authentic publication URL.
underlying_mechanism: Draft manuscripts often contain placeholder links or copied template URLs that fail verification.
incident_context: Discovered placeholder GitHub link attached to an IBM Statistical Machine Translation citation.

generalized_heuristic: When an epistemic audit flags shorthand in-text citations or missing parent containers, treat the audit feedback as an iterative refinement signal: re-read the raw reference, query search grounding/Cargo Hold, and write the complete, un-truncated vector node into the section.
underlying_mechanism: Downstream Vector DB ingestion requires exhaustive, un-truncated bibliographic nodes to preserve context.
incident_context: Iterative closed-loop revisions during Chapter 1-4 Silver assembly passes.

generalized_heuristic: When a target URL returns a 404 or redirect loop, use search grounding to locate the current canonical URL or direct PDF repository link and update the node.
underlying_mechanism: Web assets decay and restructure over time, leaving dead pointers in manuscript drafts.
incident_context: Resolving dead library budget links to direct PDF report URLs.

generalized_heuristic: Every expanded node requires an authentic, verifiable live URL. If a reference cannot be resolved after initial CrossRef and search grounding, stop immediately and prompt the Author rather than entering infinite speculative search loops.
underlying_mechanism: Unanchored citations cannot be invented; speculative multi-turn search loops exhaust model context without gaining ground truth.
incident_context: Author Directive: Mandatory URL Resolution & Token Preservation Rule.

generalized_heuristic: Decompose citation strings, author lists, and bibliographic metadata strictly via LLM semantic comprehension with structured schemas or official API responses. Regular expressions must never be used for bibliographic decomposition.
underlying_mechanism: Bibliographic strings have diverse, unpredictable human formats with parentheticals, punctuation, and abbreviations that break regular expressions.
incident_context: Author Directive (/learn): Prohibition of regex for citation parsing per ADR-012.
